name: Social Democracy
summary: Social democracy seeks social justice through democratic reform rather than revolution. It accepts a market economy but subordinates it to political control, building a universal welfare state, strong unions and collective bargaining, progressive taxation and regulation. It is internationalist, secular and socially progressive, and treats pragmatic gradual change within parliamentary institutions as the path to a more equal society.
scope: Mainstream contemporary social democracy as represented by the Socialist International's 1989 Stockholm Declaration and the parties of the PES (2024 manifesto), in the revisionist lineage of Eduard Bernstein and the post-war Nordic model, interpreted through Sheri Berman's scholarship. It excludes democratic socialists who aim to abolish capitalism and treats the Third Way as a market-friendly variant within the family rather than its centre.

universal-healthcare.rationale: A universal welfare state with public health care is the signature social-democratic achievement; the PES calls universal access to health care a fundamental right.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Social democrats campaign for decent and rising minimum wages, but Nordic parties rely on collective bargaining rather than large statutory increases, so support is real but not maximal.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Markets are accepted as useful engines of innovation, but the Socialist International holds that the market alone can never secure social goals and needs democratic steering in a mixed economy.

public-ownership.rationale: The tradition supports public property within a mixed economy and public provision of utilities and rail, but since Bad Godesberg and the Third Way nationalisation is treated as one tool among many rather than a goal.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Progressive redistribution is central, and the PES manifesto says the ultra-rich, capital and the wealthiest individuals must pay their fair share through effective taxes.

unions-good.rationale: Social democracy grew out of the labour movement; its programs affirm the right to organise and strike and make collective bargaining a pillar of the model.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property is accepted but treated as subordinate to social goals; the Socialist International says neither private nor state ownership by itself guarantees justice, so ownership is a means, not a near-absolute right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Regulating capitalism in the public interest is the core of the ideology, and current programs call for regulating financial markets, Big Tech and tax avoidance by large corporations.

cut-welfare.rationale: The welfare state is the central project of social democracy, and the PES explicitly rejects austerity; the dependency argument is a right-wing critique it opposes.

worker-ownership.rationale: Social democrats back cooperatives and co-determination, but they accept private firms in a mixed economy and do not make collective worker ownership of all businesses a goal, which is what separates them from market socialists.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Social-democratic governments have passed counter-terror surveillance laws, while their programs also stress privacy and civil liberties, so adherents are genuinely divided.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from party practice: Nordic social democrats have been restrictive on drugs while some parties (Portugal, Germany on cannabis) liberalised; the mainstream leans against full legalisation of all recreational drugs.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: European social democrats support hate-speech laws; the PES pledges to protect everyone from hate speech and to make illegal offline speech illegal online.

strong-leader.rationale: Social democracy defines itself through pluralist parliamentary democracy and free elections, and its formation was a rejection of authoritarian shortcuts.

state-harmful.rationale: The democratic state is the main instrument of social democracy; Berman stresses its belief in the primacy of politics over the economy.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed in the core texts; inferred from the strict gun laws social-democratic governments maintain and their emphasis on public safety.

empower-police-military.rationale: Older SI documents stress disarmament, while the 2024 PES manifesto supports a stronger European defence industry and Europol; adherents split on whether more funding and authority are needed.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Contested: Swedish social democrats pioneered criminalising the purchase of sex and the PES stresses fighting sexual exploitation, while some parties (e.g. German SPD) legalised it.

decide-locally.rationale: Social democrats value local government and decentralised provision, but their universal welfare state depends on national standards and redistribution, so they reject maximal localism.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian, welfare-oriented approach to social problems and the rehabilitative penal systems of Nordic social-democratic states.

traditional-family.rationale: Self-described feminist parties that support diverse families and women's independence reject the claim that the traditional family is the foundation of society.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Equality for LGBTIQ people is an explicit program commitment, and social-democratic governments led many marriage-equality reforms.

abortion-legal.rationale: The PES demands free and full access to sexual and reproductive health and rights so that women control their own bodies.

more-religion-public.rationale: Social democracy is secular in orientation: it protects freedom of belief and rejects religious fundamentalism, without seeking a larger public role for religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Social democrats commit to equal rights for all races and zero tolerance for racism, though their emphasis is on anti-discrimination law more than redress for historical wrongs.

gender-social-construct.rationale: As self-described feminists who treat gender roles and gaps as political products to be changed, adherents lean toward this view, though the texts do not state it as theory.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Berman links social democracy's success to communal solidarity and national belonging, while today's PES emphasises diversity and inclusion; communitarian and cosmopolitan wings split.

gradual-change.rationale: Gradualism is the defining trait: Bernstein argued for steady reform through democratic institutions rather than sudden upheaval.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The PES calls well-managed migration an opportunity and defends asylum rights, but some member parties (notably the Danish) have embraced restriction, so opposition is moderate.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Internationalism is core: the SI calls strengthening the United Nations an important step, and the PES wants a reformed UN and more EU capacity to act.

free-trade.rationale: Social democrats support open trade but insist it must carry labour and environmental standards and that its losers need protection; they deny it automatically benefits everyone.

nation-first.rationale: International solidarity and multilateral cooperation are founding values, though social democrats also defend national and European strategic interests.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Mainstream social democrats supported humanitarian interventions and back military aid to Ukraine, while the SI stresses peace and conflict prevention first.

open-borders.rationale: The PES wants humane asylum and legal pathways but also controlled external borders and effective returns, not open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Social democrats seek green growth and a just transition; the PES speaks of securing growth while decarbonising rather than limiting it.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The PES promises a Green Deal with no pause, climate neutrality by 2050 at the latest and a fully renewable energy mix, all driven by public investment.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The SI insists technology must be brought under democratic social control; social democrats see political action, not technology alone, as the solution.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Genuinely split: Swedish and French social democrats have backed nuclear power while the German SPD phased it out, and the PES aims at a completely renewable energy mix.

revolution-justified.rationale: Social democracy was born from rejecting revolutionary strategy in favour of democratic reform, though adherents back democratic uprisings against dictatorships.

experts-over-public.rationale: Inferred from its commitment to democratic participation and control; social democrats value expertise in administration but place final authority with voters.

central-planning.rationale: Modern social democracy rejects command economies and bureaucratic state control, favouring a regulated mixed market economy.

socialized-markets.rationale: Social democrats accept privately owned firms within a mixed economy, so they reject the market-socialist condition that only worker- or publicly owned firms make markets acceptable.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not a social-democratic priority; they rely on broad progressive taxes on income, capital and wealth and would not replace them with a single land tax.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Taxing capital and the wealthiest fits social-democratic redistribution, but practice varies (Sweden's social democrats abolished inheritance tax in 2004).

basic-income.rationale: Social democrats favour work-centred welfare, adequate minimum income schemes and job guarantees rather than an unconditional payment to every adult.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Nordic social democrats historically preferred open trade cushioned by welfare and labour-market policy over tariffs, though the PES wants protection from unfair competition.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The PES calls for a public Investment Plan to reindustrialise Europe, a Made in Europe strategy and strategic autonomy in key supplies.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Social democrats support small firms and cooperatives, but they pursue equality mainly through the welfare state and public services rather than spreading ownership; they are indifferent to this distributist goal.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Social democracy accepts wage labour and markets and seeks fair wages and labour rights within them, not their abolition.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Keynesian macroeconomic management by the state is closely tied to social democracy, which opposes leaving money to the market.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Tripartite social corporatism was central to the Nordic model, but social democrats insist on autonomous unions and employers and do not want bodies that fix prices.

one-party-rule.rationale: Social democracy requires pluralism and free choice between political alternatives and split from communism over this point.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Many social-democratic parties govern contentedly under constitutional monarchies (Scandinavia, Spain, UK), while their egalitarian principles push some toward republicanism.

democracy-best.rationale: Political democracy is the foundation of the SI declaration, and Bernstein made democratisation the path to socialism.

direct-votes.rationale: Social democrats are parliamentary parties working through representatives and organised interests; referendums are used occasionally but not favoured as the main mechanism.

workers-councils.rationale: Social democrats chose parliamentary democracy over council rule when the movement split from communism after 1917.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not in the core texts; inferred from social democrats' commitment to national solidarity and the stance of parties such as the Spanish PSOE against unilateral secession.

natural-rulers.rationale: Its egalitarian and democratic premises reject the idea of a naturally fit ruling class.

political-violence-never.rationale: The SI condemns violent ways of handling conflict and the movement is committed to peaceful reform, though it supports armed defence against aggression.

war-builds-character.rationale: The SI says peace is more than the absence of war and promotes disarmament and conflict prevention; glorifying war is alien to the tradition.

separate-church-state.rationale: Social democrats are secular and protect freedom of belief, but have lived with established churches in Nordic states, so they agree without making strict separation a priority.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The SI explicitly rejects religious fundamentalism and grounds law in democracy and human rights.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Social democrats see justice and security as public goods provided by a democratic state.

military-superiority.rationale: The tradition favours common security and multilateral collective defence over seeking superiority, though modern parties support NATO and stronger European defence.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The SI demands equal rights for all races, ethnic groups and nations, and the PES calls migrant-background citizens part of society.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Revisionists like Bernstein dropped the catastrophe theory and class-struggle determinism, and Berman sees this rejection of historical materialism as key to social democracy.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Social democrats go beyond equal opportunity, seeking compensation for social inequalities and narrower pay gaps, without demanding strict equality of outcome.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred from SI commitments to equal rights for peoples and Nordic social democrats' support for Sami rights; the texts do not specifically address land authority.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The SI supports debt cancellation and fairer North-South relations, but mainstream social democrats have not endorsed formal reparations; they are split.

civilizational-union.rationale: Social democrats back union based on shared democratic values (the EU), not on religion or civilisational identity, which they associate with the right.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Solidarity is a core value; social democracy treats the pursuit of self-interest as something to be channelled and limited, not a moral good.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Berman stresses communal solidarity and the Third Way linked rights to responsibilities, but the SI centres individual rights; adherents balance rather than rank the two.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Inferred from PES pledges to protect biodiversity, ecosystems and animal welfare; social democracy's ecology is mostly framed around human wellbeing.

limit-population.rationale: Social democrats emphasise reproductive rights and development rather than active population control.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Social democracy is a product of the industrial labour movement and seeks to spread the gains of industrial progress, not reject them.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The SI wants democratic control over the introduction of new technologies and the PES ties change to a just transition, so disruption for its own sake is resisted.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed; social democrats combine personal freedom with insistence on social control of technology and equal access, so they have no settled view.

algorithmic-government.rationale: The PES insists on a human in control principle and warns that algorithmic management must not undermine democracy.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The PES stresses privacy, but social-democratic governments have also sought lawful access for security agencies; adherents are split.

restore-past-order.rationale: Social democracy is a progressive, reformist project focused on improving the present and future, not restoring a lost order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Bernstein's focus on present tasks over final aims, and later Third Way pragmatism, make social democrats favour tested results while keeping core values.

direct-action.rationale: Social democracy is defined by pursuing change through parliamentary democracy and gradual reform instead of revolution.

means-match-ends.rationale: The Socialist International says democracy and human rights are not simply means to socialist ends but the very substance of those ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Social democrats see economic growth and technology, steered democratically, as the basis of social progress.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Social democrats accept a modern specialised economy and seek better conditions and lifelong learning within it, not the end of specialisation; inferred.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Social democracy pays incomes from work in a market economy and meets needs through a universal welfare state; it has abandoned the goal of full distribution by need.

production-for-use.rationale: Social democrats subordinate markets to social and ecological goals and keep public services out of the market, while accepting profit-driven production in a mixed economy.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Since Bernstein's revisionism social democrats have dropped the Marxist theory of exploitation and accept profit in a regulated market, while defending workers through unions.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Social democracy rejects any dictatorship, condemning Stalinism's crimes and insisting that socialism is impossible without democracy.

collective-farming.rationale: Social democrats support cooperatives of farmers but have left farming to individual owners in a mixed economy; inferred from the Nordic model and the SI's mixed-economy stance.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Social democrats rejected the Marxist catastrophe theory and pursue peace through common security and international institutions, not by abolishing capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Progressive taxation funding a universal welfare state is a defining social-democratic commitment.

harm-principle.rationale: Social democrats have often restricted self-regarding conduct, as with Nordic alcohol monopolies, restrictive drug policy and criminalising the purchase of sex, though some parties are more permissive.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Social democrats defend collective rights such as collective bargaining and equal rights for cultures and nations within society alongside individual rights.

conscription.rationale: Nordic social democrats have kept or restored conscription; Sweden's Social Democratic government reactivated it in 2017 on a gender-equal basis.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Democratic participation is at the heart of social democracy, which sees political power, not exit, as the way to hold the powerful to account.

state-as-business.rationale: Social democrats insist on the primacy of politics over markets and see citizens as members of a democratic community with social rights, not customers.

media-academia-power.rationale: Social democrats worry more about concentrated economic power than about universities and the press, which they defend as pluralist institutions; inferred.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Social democrats are committed to equal rights for all races and ethnic groups and to equal opportunity, and attribute group gaps to social conditions; inferred, as they do not address the genetic question.

organic-representation.rationale: Social democracy is a party-based parliamentary tradition, though the Nordic model adds corporatist bargaining between unions, employers and the state.

total-state.rationale: The Socialist International holds that democracy is pluralist by nature and condemns totalitarian rule.

national-rebirth.rationale: Social democrats are internationalist and reformist and reject nationalist narratives of decay and rebirth, though Berman notes they appeal to national community; inferred.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The Socialist International commits to peace, disarmament and international law, and opposes conquest.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Social democrats want authority grounded in democratic law and accountable offices; inferred from their commitment to democracy and the rule of law.

bound-labor.rationale: Social democracy grew out of the labour movement's fight for free and protected labour and treats forced labour as a human rights violation.

universal-morality.rationale: The Socialist International grounds its program in universal and inalienable human rights, though it frames them historically rather than as natural law.

single-common-good.rationale: The Socialist International holds that democracy is pluralist by nature, and social democracy has built compromises between classes and interests rather than one rational plan.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The Socialist International, which includes Israeli member parties, backs two sovereign democratic states, Israel and Palestine, though it frames Israel as a democracy for all its citizens rather than stressing its Jewish character.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Social democrats favour inclusive, civic citizenship and equal rights for all residents rather than citizenship by ancestry; inferred.

revive-national-language.rationale: Social democrats support minority language and cultural rights but are indifferent to making a revived language the state language; inferred.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The Stockholm Declaration calls for worker participation and joint decision-making at company and workplace level, self-managed cooperatives and substantial involvement by workers in economic decisions.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the Declaration's right to education and its preference for public provision of social services, so social democrats generally fund public schools directly.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the Declaration's commitment to full employment and its call for the state to regulate the market, with post-war social democrats accepting countercyclical borrowing, though some parties favour fiscal discipline.

economic-freedom.rationale: Social democrats accept a market economy but hold that politics must control it, and Berman's primacy-of-politics thesis has democratic choice shaping markets rather than depending on unregulated ones.

rule-by-example.rationale: Inferred from its commitment to parliamentary democracy and a rule-bound welfare state delivered through legislation and collective bargaining, not rulers' personal virtue; no source addresses rule by moral example directly.

national-self-determination.rationale: Social democrats back peoples' self-determination in practice, as in the two-state solution endorsed by Socialist International members, though they favour multilateral and European integration over nation-state primacy.

force-without-un.rationale: Social democrats are internationalist and back the UN and international law, so they favour force abroad only with UN or broad international authorization.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Inferred from its secular, evidence-driven reformism and the Stockholm Declaration's rejection of religious fundamentalism, but it accepts religious members and does not make reason the sole guide.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Social democracy builds universal welfare on solidarity and the PES defends migrants rights, but some member parties, notably the Danish, back citizens-first limits; inferred from its universalism.

positive-liberty.rationale: The Stockholm Declaration ties freedom to security and social rights, and the PES manifesto stresses wages, health and housing as conditions of a free life.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Universal welfare is core, but some parties, as in the Nordic activation model, attach work conditions, so adherents are split.

class-collaboration.rationale: Bernstein rejected class polarisation, and the Nordic model relies on collective bargaining and corporatist cooperation between unions and employers.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Inferred: social democrats fund public culture and libraries as part of the welfare state and do not call for discarding them.

dominated-front.rationale: Inferred: social democracy is internationalist and works through the UN and North-South partnership, not a bloc against the West.

workers-nation.rationale: The Stockholm Declaration and PES manifesto are internationalist and stress cross-border solidarity.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The PES manifesto commits to feminism and gender equality.

ban-interest.rationale: Social democracy accepts a market economy with a mixed economy and regulation, not a prohibition of lending.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The Stockholm Declaration and PES manifesto commit to equality and combat racism and hate speech.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Bernstein and Berman's account stress that democratic politics can steer markets, so the state is not simply a ruling-class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Social democrats commit to a climate transition and green investment, though workers in energy sectors temper opposition.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The PES stresses inclusion and integration with respect for diversity rather than giving up one's culture.

elite-replacement.rationale: Social democrats defend humane migration policy and oppose hate speech, and reject this conspiracy theory; inferred from the PES manifesto.

proportional-representation.rationale: Social democratic parties historically supported PR for working-class representation and it is common in the Nordic model; inferred, not a stated principle.

national-mission.rationale: Social democracy is internationalist, committed to the UN, peace and cooperation, not to exporting a national model.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The PES manifesto is explicitly feminist and calls for tackling structural gender inequality.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Social democrats are governing-party institutionalists who defend democratic politics, though they criticize elites captured by wealth; inferred.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: The Declaration upholds human rights and individual dignity; the Nordic sterilization programs are now repudiated.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Rule of law and human rights are core commitments, so accountability for state abuses fits; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Social democracy rests on a welfare state and a mixed economy under democratic political control, the opposite of a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The Stockholm Declaration and PES manifesto commit to equality and against racial discrimination.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Declaration of Principles and PES manifesto make equal dignity and equal rights central values.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Inferred: social democrats reject revolution and pursue gradual national reform within parliamentary democracy.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Inferred: the PES backs a two-state settlement and Israel's security, and members are split on the colonial label.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to equal rights and women's equality under common law; the tradition has not addressed personal-law systems directly.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to freedom of conscience and religion; the tradition has not addressed conversion law directly.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred: social democrats favour animal-welfare rules but have not backed bans based on religious reverence.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from the movement's secularism and its universal public education; practice varies in Europe.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Inferred: Bernstein and the Declaration put democracy first, so a growing security state is not accepted.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Democracy and popular sovereignty are the core of the Declaration of Principles and Bernstein's revisionism.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Social democracy is a rationalist, reformist tradition that relies on evidence and expertise in policy, though it is not centrally concerned with the question; inferred.

trade-surplus.rationale: Social democrats favour open, rules-based trade with social protections and do not treat export surpluses as a national goal; inferred from the PES and Socialist International internationalism.

population-transfer.rationale: Social democrats defend human rights and the rights of minorities, and the PES and Socialist International oppose expulsion and forced displacement.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Social democrats accept that states may use force, including in defence of others and under international law, and do not hold an absolute non-aggression principle; inferred.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Social democrats accept markets as engines of innovation but hold that solidarity, public institutions and the welfare state drive social progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Social democrats treat democracy as defensible, and the SPD helped shape Germany's militant-democracy provisions, though many are cautious about bans; the documented majority view is to allow it.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Social democrats link freedom to social conditions and security from dependence, as in the Stockholm Declaration's view of freedom, though the republican term is not theirs; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: Social democrats are committed to constitutional, pluralist democracy with checks and rule of law, though they stress a strong democratic state able to act.

vanguard-party.rationale: Social democracy since Bernstein rejects revolution and vanguardism in favour of democratic reform through parliament and mass organizations.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Social democrats want policy to reduce inequality and protect the most vulnerable through universal welfare and progressive taxation, but they favour universal programmes over strict priority.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Social democrats prioritise a strong public housing sector and have often opposed selling it off, though some parties accepted it; contested, so low.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Social democracy rests on strong unions and collective bargaining and accepts regulated, lawful strikes, so it resists new restrictions.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The welfare state and primacy of politics assume poverty is shaped by social and political arrangements, not by population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The PES manifesto stresses equality, anti-discrimination and hate-speech action, and the Stockholm Declaration defends pluralism.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Social democracy works through representative parliamentary democracy; lottery is not discussed, so inferred.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The Stockholm Declaration puts democracy, pluralism and human rights first, so suspending legal protections is rejected.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Social democrats accept market intervention for social ends and have backed price caps in crises; not stated for food, so inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: The Declaration commits to democracy and pluralism, including a free press, so government or party control of media is rejected.

party-commands-army.rationale: Social democratic parties accept constitutional civilian control of the armed forces by the state, as in Sweden.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The PES backs migrant integration and citizenship access, so long waits are disfavoured; not stated precisely, so inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Social democrats favour reasonable pay for office and no cult of wealth, but do not demand average-worker pay; adherents are split and the sources are silent.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Parties in the family expect broad unity in parliament yet permit conscience votes and free debate; adherents are genuinely split and the sources do not address it.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The PES manifesto backs deeper European integration and shared institutions that bind member states.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Social democracy is parliamentary: government answers to the legislature, and executive command without legislative approval is incompatible with its parliamentary democracy.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Social democrats are secular and favour pluralism and democratic institutions over hierarchical church rule; inferred, as the family seldom addresses church governance.

clerical-rule.rationale: The Stockholm Declaration stresses secular, pluralist democracy and religious freedom, so clerical rule is rejected.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Social democrats supported national defence in 1914 and the Nordic model includes conscription; revisionism rejects revolutionary defeatism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Social democrats defend free expression though the PES backs hate-speech law; art censorship for moral character is rejected as illiberal.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Parliamentary systems in the family mostly have no president and adherents have no common line on term limits; inferred as split.

recall-officials.rationale: Democratic accountability is central, but most social democracies rely on elections and confidence votes rather than recall; inferred at low confidence.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Social democratic governments and the PES back NATO and collective defence, and Sweden's Social Democrats reactivated conscription; ending alliances is not their position.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Social democracy accepts rental markets and regulates them with tenant protections and social housing; a ban on renting is far from its program.

people-in-arms.rationale: They support organised state defence forces under democratic control, and Sweden reinstated conscription; an armed citizenry in place of an army is not a social democratic aim.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: No programmatic view; the tradition is urban and labour-based, so it would not call rural life morally healthier; inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The Socialist International accepts existing borders in cases like the two-state solution, but members differ on particular partitions; no stated position.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Social democrats value education and expertise and would reject the claim that the educated are out of touch; inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The PES program stresses anti-racism, equality and respect for diversity, which implies no culture is inferior.

death-penalty.rationale: The PES and Socialist International oppose the death penalty everywhere, including for terrorism.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The PES program backs feminism and gender equality, including in education, and social democrats broadly support school sex education.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Secular and committed to scientific education, social democrats keep religion out of science classes.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Contested within the family; the Nordic model has been restrictive on sex work while civil liberties favour freedom, so a mild lean against restriction.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The PES stresses integration and equal rights for migrants and their children, which fits birthright more than descent-only; inferred, though Denmark's party differs.

minority-language-support.rationale: The PES program supports the rights of minorities, including language and cultural rights, in public services and education.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Social democrats are secular but pluralist; exemptions for minorities are supported by some parties and opposed by others.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Socially progressive and liberal on personal life, social democrats would welcome diverse ways of living; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The Socialist International declaration backs relief for the debt burden of poor countries as part of North-South justice, though social democrats usually favor negotiated relief.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: social democrats stress democratic, gradual reform and a mixed economy, not wholesale ownership change as a condition of independence.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Inferred from Bernstein and the Nordic model, which pursue change through existing parliamentary institutions rather than constitutional rupture.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Democracy, pluralism and civil liberties are fundamental to social democracy, which rejects authoritarian development.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The Stockholm Declaration commits to international solidarity and a fairer North-South order, and Nordic social democrats have long given large aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred: the PES manifesto favors European and alliance-based defence and multilateral disarmament over national nuclear forces.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred: social democratic parties hold both parliamentary and presidential systems and no common line exists.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Inferred: post-war social democrats favored government direction of the economy, while modern parties accepted central bank independence, so adherents are split.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Socialist International delegations, Israeli and Palestinian included, back a negotiated two-state solution, which implies territorial compromise.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: A mixed economy where markets are subordinated to political control and social purposes implies that property serves the community.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Inferred: social democrats rejected Soviet communism as dictatorship, but not by calling it state capitalist, and the label is not part of their program.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Social democratic parties back strong environmental regulation as part of green transition programmes, though the precautionary principle is not their own doctrine.

collective-defense.rationale: European social democratic parties support NATO and EU mutual-defence commitments, as in Sweden and Finland joining NATO; inferred from their internationalism.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The Socialist International stresses self-determination and international law; inferred application to annexation.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Social democracy is secular but upholds religious freedom and the autonomy of churches within the law; inferred.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Nordic social democracies live with constitutional monarchies or ceremonial presidents who stand above party politics; inferred.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Social democrats favour democratic consent and international law, so oppose force against an unwilling region; inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Regional autonomy and devolution are accepted within democratic states; inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Social democracy is secular and parliamentary; a sacred ruler of divine descent contradicts both.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Progressive taxation is a core instrument of social democratic redistribution.

character-from-environment.rationale: Social democrats stress equal opportunity, education and public services to shape life chances; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Constitutional democracy and the rule of law bind rulers; Bernstein sought change through parliamentary means.

space-expansion.rationale: No social democratic position; adherents are split and it is not a defining issue.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Its commitment to democracy favours government by the many rather than any aristocratic element; inferred.

leader-cult.rationale: Leader cults contradict social democracy's democratic and pluralist principles.

equal-parenting.rationale: Nordic social democracies emphasise gender equality and shared parenting; inferred.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Bernstein's revisionism rejected the Marxist expectation of sharpening class conflict in favour of gradual reform, and modern social democrats do not expect a socialist order to be threatened by its own party leaders.

land-redistribution.rationale: Social democracy regulates and taxes property rather than expropriating it; inferred from its reformist, rights-respecting approach to property.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from the movement's human-rights commitments and its stated support for a negotiated settlement that addresses refugees; it is not a defining position.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Internationalist, rights-based social democracy rejects territorial claims grounded in ethnic kinship.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Social democrats are secular and committed to freedom of conscience and human rights.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compulsory dress codes for women conflict with the movement's commitment to gender equality and individual freedom.

common-currency.rationale: Social-democratic parties in the PES back European integration and the euro, though some adherents criticise its austerity rules.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred: social democracy builds unity on shared democratic values and civic institutions, not on common ancestry or language family.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from the pluralist, minority-rights stance of social democracy and the Austro-Marxist social-democratic tradition of cultural autonomy; adherents rarely address it directly.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from the movement's emphasis on equal rights and anti-discrimination within existing states.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Bernstein revised the strict Marxist materialism and contemporary social democrats credit both economic conditions and ideas; adherents are split.

ban-cartels.rationale: Regulating markets and curbing concentrated economic power is a core part of subordinating the market economy to political control.

no-bailouts.rationale: Social democrats generally accept public rescues to protect jobs and financial stability, usually with conditions; inferred from their pro-state-intervention stance.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Social democracy is committed to liberal democracy with entrenched rights and judicial independence, so it does not want majorities free of constitutional limits.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender equality is central, and social-democratic parties commonly use quotas and parity rules for their own lists and bodies.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Social democracy is internationalist and favours cooperation and regulated trade over autarky.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding labor and environmental standards in trade deals are a standard social-democratic demand to stop a race to the bottom.

moral-incentives.rationale: Social democracy keeps a market economy with wages and material incentives; inferred from its acceptance of markets.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Social democracy pursues gradual change through democratic institutions and rejects revolutionary violence.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Equality of opportunity and democratic equality are core, so inherited titles and privileges are opposed, though it is not a live campaign.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred from the internationalist, pluralist outlook of the Stockholm Declaration and PES; not a stated position.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Stockholm Declaration backs self-determination, the UN and North-South equality, which rule out rule over other peoples for their supposed benefit.

patriotic-education.rationale: Social democrats are internationalist and secular and tend to favour civic over nationalist education; inferred, with some national-minded parties dissenting.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The PES backs anti-discrimination and positive action for disadvantaged groups, so most adherents would keep race-conscious measures, though class-based ones are favoured by some.

public-money-creation.rationale: Social democrats accept a mixed economy with central banks and regulated banking, not public monopoly of money creation; inferred.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Bernstein rejected the collapse theory and argued capitalism adapts through credit and cartels, the founding revisionist claim of the tradition.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred from the internationalism and anti-imperial stance of the Socialist International; not directly addressed.

delink-world-market.rationale: The Stockholm Declaration and PES manifesto favour fairer trade rules and cooperation between North and South, not delinking.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Internationalist solidarity and the Declaration's North-South equity assume common worker interests; Bernstein also rejected class polarisation.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The PES manifesto demands strong anti-discrimination law and action against hate speech, and social democrats defend such law as central to equality.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Social democrats support human rights and pluralism, but Nordic traditions rely on parliamentary sovereignty, so the support for entrenchment is inferred and mixed.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from the Stockholm Declaration's support for self-determination and North-South justice; treaty validity is not addressed.

elective-rulers.rationale: Social democrats favour democracy but Nordic and British parties accept constitutional monarchies; inferred as split.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from its commitment to majority rule in parliamentary democracy alongside minority rights.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from its commitment to constitutional democracy and defence of democracy against dictatorship.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Social democracy pursues change through parliamentary institutions and democratic reform, so parliament is the seat of lawmaking authority.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred from mainstream progressive and European welfare positions; the sources do not address it.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from European social-democratic support for animal welfare rules rather than bans on use.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Social democrats back solidarity through universal rights and taxation, not paternal duty of the privileged; inferred as split.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The tradition treats democratic political participation as the means of social justice and rejects withdrawal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not a mainstream social-democratic claim; inferred from its reformist, non-Marxist outlook.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred from reformist rejection of Marxist class-power theory, though adherents recognise cultural influence.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred from the Stockholm Declaration's call for a fairer world economy, short of an extraction theory.

native-born-offices.rationale: Internationalism and equality of citizens make reserving offices for the native-born contrary to its principles.

party-own-road.rationale: Inferred from the Socialist International's membership of independent national parties.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from its support for development aid and international solidarity.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred from its internationalism and commitment to peace and existing borders.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from equal citizenship; it supports indigenous rights and redress but not descent-based leadership.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred from social democrats' historic opposition to fascism and the postwar democratic settlement.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred from its democratic opposition to both fascist and communist dictatorship.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred from its progressive, egalitarian outlook and the mainstream historical view.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from its progressive outlook; adherents are mixed on removal.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred from universalist equality and welfare commitments.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Adherents support protection for all victims but disagree on symmetry; inferred as split.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from its universal commitment to democracy and human rights.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred from its commitment to civilian democratic control of the military.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from welfare-state support for valuing and funding care services.

filial-duty.rationale: The welfare state aims to replace dependence on family with public support, and the programs set no filial duty; inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: Social democracy rests on parliamentary democracy, though it values a merit-based civil service; examination-only selection of posts is not its view. Inferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: PES programs back strategic autonomy and screening of foreign investment in key sectors, though support is not strong.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Secular, socially progressive parties back personal freedom in family law.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Social democracy works through representative parliamentary democracy with fixed terms, not imperative mandates and instant recall.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Social democrats defend universal public pensions funded by shared contributions and taxes against privatised accounts.

land-use-tenure.rationale: A mixed economy keeps private property, including land, under regulation and taxation, rather than land held in common.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary control of the budget is basic to the democratic institutions social democracy defends.

single-official-language.rationale: Pluralist and internationalist, and the PES stresses cultural and linguistic diversity in Europe; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The PES backs the EU single market and free movement, and no party program seeks bans on foreign land ownership; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The PES backs anti-discrimination measures and equality, though many parties weigh intent and outcomes differently; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Parties stress sustainability and quality of life over consumption, though they support consumer protection and growth; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The movement commits to the UN and peace and generally opposes covert arming of rebels; inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Social democracy upholds UN principles, sovereignty and peace, so force to keep an ally in a bloc is rejected.

corporate-influence.rationale: Curbing the power of money over democratic politics fits the primacy of politics over markets that the PES and Stockholm Declaration stress.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred: social democrats favour open, internationalist civil society and would see such restrictions as a risk to pluralism, though some accept transparency rules.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred: family policy is a welfare-state staple, but the tradition is pro-migration and internationalist, so it would not frame incentives as a substitute for immigration.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from internationalism and free movement within the EU; housing policy is pursued through public provision and regulation, not residency bars.

job-guarantee.rationale: Full employment is a core goal and active public job programmes are part of the Nordic model, though a universal guarantee is not a formal party position.

democratic-peace.rationale: The Stockholm Declaration ties peace to the spread of democracy and human rights and to a strengthened UN.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred: social democrats work within parliamentary legality and stress the legitimacy of democratic law, so they reject the claim as a general principle.

non-intervention.rationale: The Socialist International backs the UN, international law and human rights, which allow collective action in extreme cases such as atrocities.

industrial-unions.rationale: Industrial and general unions dominate the Nordic and German labour movements, though the sources don't address the question directly.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Pluralism, equality and opposition to racism and discrimination are core commitments, so conspiracy claims against minorities are rejected.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred: social democrats back equal rights for all family forms and partnership laws, not the abolition of legal marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Transparent, accountable democratic government is a stated aim of the Declaration and PES programme.

local-production.rationale: Inferred: the tradition favours trade within regulated markets and international cooperation over localism as a principle.

informal-organisation.rationale: Social democracy is built on permanent parties, unions and parliamentary organisation, as the sources describe.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The movement supports binding international law and institutions such as the UN and ICC and European integration, so it rejects national precedence.

religious-nation.rationale: The Declaration affirms secularism and freedom of religion and belief, so a nation defined by religion is rejected.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from the Declaration's internationalism and commitment to equal sovereign states under the UN, which excludes tribute and ritual submission.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Social democracy builds on solidarity and redistribution, so pooling revenue by need fits more than regional retention; the program does not address regions directly.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Social democrats accept a mixed economy with private enterprise, so 'means of production held in common' is only partly their view while personal property is plainly private.

defeat-communism.rationale: The Declaration stresses peace, detente and democracy; I infer social democrats oppose communist dictatorship but favour coexistence and engagement over a campaign to defeat it.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Mixed provision inside a publicly funded system is common in contemporary social-democratic governments and the Third Way variant, though some adherents want state delivery.

religion-illusion.rationale: The Declaration treats religion as a private matter within a secular, pluralist order; the materialist claim that religion fades is not the party line, and I infer disagreement at low confidence.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Social democrats accept the market economy and wealth creation and Bernstein held capitalism was adapting, which supports crediting it with progress.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Social democrats pursue equality by law and policy within the existing market economy, which implies reform without transforming the system.

socialized-care.rationale: The PES program backs public childcare and care services; I infer support for public provision of care work, with less on housework.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the PES program's support for linguistic and cultural diversity and open, plural democracy.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from social democratic support for indigenous rights and the rule of law, matching its answers on indigenous authority and colonial treaties.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Social democrats favour a mixed economy and national welfare states; small self-governing communes are not part of the Declaration's program, so I infer disagreement.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the program's commitment to equality of minorities and human rights, which excludes steering majority settlement into minority regions.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Social democracy is historically defined as a third way between laissez-faire capitalism and Soviet communism, a mixed economy under democratic control.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred: its internationalist, universalist principles give no priority to historical or religious land claims; the Madrid resolution backs a negotiated settlement based on mutual rights.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Inferred from its democratic, humanist principles in the Stockholm Declaration; no social-democratic party endorses denial.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The Stockholm Declaration stresses human rights and equal dignity, which social democrats apply against criminalising homosexuality.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Stockholm Declaration makes political democracy, pluralism and human rights central.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Social democracy is secular and rights-based, and does not support state punishment of blasphemy.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Stockholm Declaration condemns colonialism and stresses equal rights among nations.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: it is an Islamic doctrine social democrats do not hold, and the Madrid resolution calls for peaceful settlement.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Social democracy holds that legitimacy comes from democratic elections, not religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The Stockholm Declaration endorses democratic participation and influence in workplaces and communities, though through representative institutions and bargaining.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred from its equality and anti-discrimination goals; the sources do not use the intersectional framing.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from its rights-based, anti-discrimination stance; not documented in the sources opened.

assisted-dying.rationale: Adherents are split and parties treat it as a matter of conscience.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Social democrats see themselves as the left's reformist wing, though the Third Way tried to combine left and right ideas.

alienated-labor.rationale: Social democracy accepts a market economy and aims to ease its harms rather than end wage labour, so adherents are split on the alienation critique.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred from its universalist, anti-discrimination principles; the sources do not discuss it.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Social democracy is secular and rests on popular sovereignty and democratic legitimacy.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Adherents are split between secular-neutrality (France, Nordic parties) and tolerance of religious dress.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from its aim to protect workers' rights and bargaining power; not discussed in the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: Social democracy subordinates a market economy to social protection, regulation and collective bargaining, which this statement describes.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Mainstream social democracy supports democratic states' defence capacity, as Sweden's conscription shows, while pursuing disarmament and peace.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from its equality and solidarity principles, which favour progressive taxation and redistribution over allowing some to grow rich first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred: social democratic parties are mostly in Western alliances such as NATO, though some favour neutrality.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Social democracy is defined by commitment to democracy, and the Stockholm Declaration grounds politics in popular sovereignty; hereditary head of state office is inferred to be rejected.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Cooperative banks exist in social-democratic countries, but the programmes favour regulated and public finance rather than mutual credit specifically; adherents are split.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Social democratic parties oppose austerity as policy, but those in government have accepted lender conditions, so the answer is a low-confidence inference.

property-franchise.rationale: Universal suffrage was won by the labour movement and is a basic democratic commitment of the Socialist International.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Gender equality and climate action are both in the programmes, but treating them as one logic of domination is not a shared doctrine; adherents are split.

reification.rationale: Revisionists since Bernstein accept markets as a useful mechanism within a regulated order, so adherents mostly reject the claim that markets distort social perception; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Concern for pluralism and for limits on concentrated economic power is common, though adherents regard formal freedoms as valuable; inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Social democracy is defined by constitutional parliamentary democracy and the rule of law, per the Stockholm Declaration and the scholarship.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Stockholm Declaration and PES manifesto reject racial discrimination and affirm equal rights.

online-participation.rationale: Parties favour broader participation and digital democracy, but the sources do not address online decisions directly; inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: Transparency and accountability are standard democratic commitments of the parties; inferred, not specifically sourced.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Social democracy champions equal rights and freedom of belief, which excludes legal limits on marriage across religions.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The programmes oppose discrimination on religion and racism; singling out minority businesses contradicts that.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Social democrats stress deepening democracy, and some parties have backed citizens' assemblies, but the family is mainly committed to parliamentary representation; inferred from its democratic principles, and adherents are divided.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The Stockholm Declaration affirms secularism and freedom of religion and the family is socially progressive, so modernising readings of religion are favoured; no source addresses reinterpretation of doctrine directly, so this is inferred.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Social democrats justify progressive taxation and regulation partly by the need to prevent economic power from undermining democracy; the Stockholm Declaration says freedom requires that economic power be democratically accountable.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Contemporary social democratic parties, including the PES, back equal rights for LGBTI people, which includes open service in the armed forces.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Social democracy is secular but liberal and pluralist; state promotion of atheism is contrary to its commitment to freedom of conscience.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Social democrats rely on the state and the rule of law, favouring prevention and rehabilitation within existing institutions rather than abolition of police and prisons.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; social democrats accept consociational arrangements in some countries but the family has no common position.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Social democracy's defining claim is that a universal state welfare system, not voluntary charity, should secure social rights, as the Stockholm Declaration and PES manifesto state.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred from its parliamentary party tradition, in which long-serving representatives are normal; the family does not campaign for term limits.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred: social democracy rests on representative parliamentary institutions and party organisation, not delegated voting.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Inferred from its internationalism and the PES's emphasis on long-term and global challenges; not an explicit statement about extinction risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Social democratic parties are committed to gender equality, and women's equal access to office is a standard social democratic position, though religious bodies are not their direct concern.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Gender equality, including equality within the family, is a core social democratic principle in the Stockholm Declaration and PES programme.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from its internationalism and commitment to inclusive citizenship.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from its regulation of markets for social justice, applied to housing.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from its acceptance of a regulated market economy, which includes intellectual property regimes.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Its commitment to democratic, secular, pluralist institutions makes drilled national-service youth movements alien to it.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from its peace and disarmament commitments, though member parties in NATO states vary.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Many social-democratic parties govern in military alliances that host foreign forces, so adherents are split.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from its human-rights and internationalist commitments.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: It accepts private capital income within a market economy but uses progressive taxation to reduce unearned inequality.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Social-democratic states such as Sweden have kept conscription and national defence, and the movement accepts defensive force.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from its internationalism and civic rather than ethnic view of the nation.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed; this is a contested academic debate on which the movement takes no position.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed; the movement supports gender equality without taking a side in this theoretical debate.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from its secular and internationalist outlook, which does not sanctify death for the nation.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Social democracy treats politics as pragmatic, secular, gradual reform, not a struggle between good and evil.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed; no position is documented.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred from its focus on using the state and institutions for reform rather than cultural renewal first.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is secular and leaves religious language to believers.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is secular and takes no position on judging religious texts.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Its internationalism and commitment to equality oppose ethnic ownership of the economy.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its internationalist, civic approach to territory.

independent-unions.rationale: Strong unions and collective bargaining are core, and the independent, member-led union is the model of the Nordic and PES tradition.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Social democrats link socialism to democracy, so rule from above is not their goal; they rarely define socialism by the question, so this is inferred.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Universal public services such as health, water and transport are central to the welfare state it builds.

second-chamber.rationale: Social democratic parties are split on bicameralism and it is not a doctrinal issue.

municipal-property.rationale: It accepts a market economy with mixed ownership and rejects abolishing private ownership in favour of local-only ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: It favours binding common institutions, as in the EU, rather than purely coordinating delegates; inferred.

family-wage.rationale: Welfare and living-wage policy are central but the gendered family wage is dated; adherents are split.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not discussed; the regulating, protective stance of the welfare state suggests keeping careful testing.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not discussed; public research funding is welcomed but ageing research is not a programme item.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not discussed; the regulatory state aims to combat tax evasion and money laundering, so untraceable payments are disfavoured; inferred.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not discussed; PES stresses online safety and accountability but also civil liberties.

person-over-state.rationale: Human dignity and individual rights sit at the centre of the Stockholm Declaration, which aims at freedom within solidarity.

spiritual-nature.rationale: It is secular and neutral on religion, so spiritual needs are neither endorsed nor rejected as a political aim.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Not discussed; practice differs between unitary and federal social democracies.

gm-crops.rationale: Not discussed; adherents vary between precaution and support for the technology.

dense-cities.rationale: PES-style climate and transport programmes favour compact, well-served cities; inferred.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Internationalist and egalitarian; the PES manifesto opposes racism and organising by race.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from its anti-racism and internationalism; not discussed.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Adherents support defence and also UN-backed or alliance-based action, as seen in Sweden and the Socialist International's statements.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Social democracy is internationalist and civic rather than ethno-linguistic in its idea of the nation, inferred from its principles.

communal-electorates.rationale: Social democrats are secular and support common citizenship and universal suffrage, so separate religious electorates are disfavoured.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Internationalist social-democratic parties treat such claims as nationalist rhetoric; the position is inferred from the Stockholm declaration's internationalism.

free-public-college.rationale: Free or low-fee public higher education is the norm in Nordic social-democratic welfare states, and the party platforms support equal access to education.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Social democratic parties back carbon pricing and green taxes alongside regulation and public investment, as in PES programmes, though they do not rely on taxes alone.

future-generations.rationale: The Stockholm Declaration treats sustainable development and protection of the environment as an obligation to future generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Social democrats back gender equality and quotas but on equal-rights grounds rather than distinct values; inferred.

arms-reduction.rationale: The Socialist International's declaration commits to disarmament and arms control, and social-democratic parties have promoted detente.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Parties favour multilateral, transparent institutions, but pragmatic governments accept confidential negotiation; inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: Modern social democracy accepts open markets and the EU single market, with regulation and taxation rather than capital controls, though some historic parties used them.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Social democrats work through accountable parliamentary states, so a state monopoly on force is inferred, though the sources do not discuss private armed groups.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Social democratic parties accepted national defence, as in Sweden's long-standing conscription system, rather than urging soldiers to refuse orders.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Strong unions and collective bargaining are core features of the social-democratic model described in the sources.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Supplementing low pay through the tax system fits the redistributive welfare state, though Nordic parties rely more on bargaining and benefits.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred as split: Third Way and European social democrats accepted fiscal rules, while others favour discretion for investment and counter-cyclical spending.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The Stockholm Declaration and PES texts favour fairer international trade, debt relief and development cooperation.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Bernstein's revisionism and social democracy reject revolution in favour of using parliamentary institutions for gradual reform.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred: social democrats favour a defined model of a regulated market economy and welfare state rather than open-ended experimentation.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred as split: modern social democracy backs green-economy tools but also regulation and public control over pricing nature.

sacred-nation.rationale: Social democracy is internationalist and secular, treating the nation as a political community rather than a sacred one.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from the preference for free or low-cost public education and reducing inequality, not from any stated position on loan cancellation.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: social democrats treat regional inequality as a matter for redistribution and cohesion policy, not as colonial-style exploitation.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to universal human dignity and rights; the sources do not discuss human nature or redesigning it.

public-service-media.rationale: The PES and the Nordic model support media freedom and pluralism, and public broadcasters are a mainstream social-democratic institution.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The sources treat religion only as a matter of pluralism and secular politics, not doctrine, so this is inferred as indifference.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from the mixed economy and market regulation the sources describe, which in Nordic and EU practice includes farm price floors and cooperative credit.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred: the movement backs multilateral disarmament, but governed social-democratic parties have mostly kept deterrence while rivals hold arms, as Sweden's 2017 conscription return shows for defence generally.

workers-own-party.rationale: Social democracy arose as the political arm of organised labour, and its parties are labour parties by origin and name.

ban-fgm.rationale: Universal human rights and women's equality are core to the PES programme, so a legal ban is the natural position; FGM itself is inferred, not named.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Gender equality before the law is a core commitment of the PES programme, which includes equal economic rights; land inheritance itself is not named.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Neither the Declaration nor the PES manifesto addresses linguistic classification, so this is inferred as indifference.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Social democrats want the political community to set rules for markets in advance, so agency regulation rather than after-the-fact private suits fits the primacy of politics.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to parliamentary democracy and secular pluralism, which leaves lawmaking to elected representatives.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred: the PES accepts binding climate rules that limit market freedoms, but it also stresses liberty, so the priority is not stated strongly.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the movement's rights and rehabilitation emphasis, which favours judicial discretion over fixed sentences.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred: the PES backs integration policies, and several governing social-democratic parties require language learning, though adherents differ.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from strong support for collective bargaining and union strength, which fits shared obligations in covered workplaces.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from the PES emphasis on inclusive democracy and wide participation.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Social democrats favour secular, pluralist states with tolerance of all beliefs, as the Stockholm Declaration's treatment of religion indicates.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The Stockholm Declaration extends democracy to economic and social life, so elections alone are not the whole of it.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the PES feminist and progressive social agenda.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from its commitment to civil liberties and pluralism.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from its universal welfare state with services and benefits as rights, rather than one means-tested payment.

women-suffrage.rationale: Equal political rights for women are basic to its democratic and feminist commitments.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from its secular outlook, though it does not name religion as a main cause.

race-social-construct.rationale: The PES manifesto opposes racism, consistent with seeing race as a social category.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The PES manifesto backs feminist policy and public institutions to advance gender equality.

notes: Contested points: nuclear power (Swedish/French vs German parties), immigration (Danish Social Democrats far more restrictive than the PES line), sex work (Nordic model vs legalisation), public ownership (strong in the post-war era, weak after the Third Way), and surveillance and encryption, where governing parties have often been more security-minded than their programs. US 'social democrats' would differ on hate-speech law and guns.
